review_scope: Bounded source/assertion review. Parent findings and gate-results supersede draft execution statements. No whole-clause certification.

decisions.review: partly confirmed; bounded coverage limit remains
decisions.basis: Current code registers type-4 fault cells at parse time inside thread-local watch scopes; interpreted pages report faults after eager evaluation and retain cells for type-1 grids evaluated later. Model assertions exercise tint transforms, image, transfer, black generation, mesh, and post-draw type-1 shading with conforming controls. This matches §7.10.5.3's three stated runtime errors where those paths actually evaluate the function. ADR 2848 explicitly records the GPU/reporting gap and overbroad low-bit image-table sampling. Those remain limits, not silently solved claims.

decisions.review: deferred premise remains accurate for GPU execution
decisions.basis: This shard found no GPU-side fault word/readback in the changed implementation; the GPU Type 4 path still does not record run-time faults. CPU-side watcher integration does not close that path. Treat this as an explicit deferred scope and do not claim complete cross-backend error reporting.

decisions.review: zero-fill premise reaffirmed; width claim corrected
decisions.basis: The primary PLRM3 §8.2 p.539 says bits shifted in are zero and both operands must be integers, so logical right-shift behavior is source-backed; however, §3.3.1 says machine integer representation can depend on CPU, and Appendix B.1 pp.738–739 labels 32-bit limits typical for Adobe implementations on 32-bit machines and says they do not necessarily apply to all implementations. Current i32 results are a local implementation choice, not a universal 32-bit mandate. The existing unit test has exact i32 expectations; the public test only checks a negative right shift becomes nonnegative, which is appropriately width-agnostic.
decisions.source: Adobe PLRM3 §3.3.1 printed p. 38; §8.2 bitshift printed p. 539; Appendix B.1/Table B.1 printed pp. 738–739; local copy hash 6b29e79e4ab64aaa61a3fb27a0f36838c01f2530362873ac316bdb493a1bab6b at /home/cl/projects/pdf-viewer/scratchpad/r1983/spec-audit/source/PLRM3.pdf; ISO §7.10.5.2 and Annex B.3.; code also independently confirms local i32 implementation: crates/pdf-colour/src/function.rs::Operator::Bitshift
residuals: Do not claim exact shift>=32 results are universal PostScript requirements.
Real shift operands are typecheck under PLRM3 §8.2, but current evaluator truncates them; malformed-operand error signaling remains unimplemented.

decisions.review: choice reaffirmed with valid-fixture coverage and bounded edge finding
decisions.basis: §7.10.2/Table 39 specifies cubic spline interpolation but no end condition. ADR 1636 chooses a tensor-product not-a-knot spline; code evaluates that choice and source-directed unit fixtures reproduce a known cubic and compare end pieces against an independent Lagrange calculation. This does not make the chosen spline normative. The same shared interpolation helper has a separate defect for nonzero spans below f32::EPSILON; the new draft covers it.

decisions.review: operator type-conversion choice not source-conformant for bitshift operands
decisions.basis: PLRM3 §8.2 bitshift specifies `int1 shift` and raises typecheck unless both operands are integers. The current evaluator calls Value::integer, which truncates a real operand; the unit test `an_integer_operator_truncates_a_real_operand` specifically expects `{ 1.5 3 bitshift }` to yield 8. This is an infallible-evaluator recovery behavior for malformed input, not the delegated operator semantics. No valid-input change is recommended by this observation alone.
